# Provider policies

Heard embeds third-party players. Each provider's terms decide where captions may be
drawn; the result is encoded in `capabilities` on the provider
(`apps/web/src/lib/providers/*`), and the watch page follows it.

## YouTube

Checked 2026-11-26 against:

- Required Minimum Functionality — https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/required-minimum-functionality
- YouTube API Services Developer Policies — https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies

### Captions over the player: not allowed

Required Minimum Functionality, "Overlays and frames":

> "You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player"

So `youtubeProvider.capabilities.allowsCaptionOverlay = false`:

- Captions render in a caption bar **directly below** the player (same `CaptionText`
  component and the user's caption settings).
- The "Over video" placement option in caption settings is hidden for YouTube; a stored
  `position: "overlay"` is ignored.
- Our own controls (caption settings, transcript download menu) open below the stage, and in
  fullscreen the settings open as a side sheet that shrinks the player instead of covering it.
  The one-time "how to share this tab" dialog is a transient modal over the whole page.
- When the player reports an error we hide the player entirely and show our message in its
  place (rather than drawing on top of it).

### Player size

> "Embedded players must have a viewport that is at least 200px by 200px."

The player is 16:9 and full-width with `min-width: 200px; min-height: 200px`. YouTube also
recommends (not requires) at least 480×270 for 16:9 players; the desktop layout exceeds that.

### Player changes / fullscreen

> "You must not make changes to the YouTube player that are not explicitly described by the API documentation."

We only use documented `playerVars` (`fs=0`, `playsinline=1`, `rel=0`, `start`, `enablejsapi`,
`origin`) and documented player methods. YouTube's own fullscreen is turned off with `fs=0`;
Heard's fullscreen button fullscreens a container that holds the untouched player plus the
caption bar underneath it, so captions stay visible.

### Open question: audio capture

Developer Policies III.I.7 says you must not "separate, isolate, or modify the audio or video
components of any YouTube audiovisual content". Heard analyses the tab's audio output with
the user's explicit permission (Chrome's tab-sharing picker) to produce captions; it doesn't
store, replay or redistribute audio, and the video keeps playing unmodified in YouTube's
player. Whether live transcription of tab audio counts as "isolating" audio is not addressed
explicitly by the policy; a hosted, public deployment should review this with counsel. The
Chrome extension (captions on youtube.com itself, no embed) is not subject to the embedded
player rules above.

### Errors

IFrame `onError` codes are mapped to friendly messages in
`apps/web/src/lib/providers/youtube/index.ts`: 2 (invalid id), 5 (HTML5 player error),
100 (removed/private), 101/150 (embedding disabled → "Open on YouTube" + Heard extension).

/**
 * Video provider abstraction. The watch page only talks to these interfaces, so adding
 * Twitch, Vimeo or direct media URLs means adding a provider — no changes to the
 * transcription code (which lives in @heard/shared and knows nothing about players).
 */

export interface ParsedVideo {
  providerId: string;
  /** Stable key for this video (used to reset state when it changes). */
  key: string;
  /** Canonical page URL on the provider's site ("Open on YouTube"). */
  canonicalUrl: string;
  /** Provider-specific data needed to embed it. */
  embed: Record<string, string | number | undefined>;
  /** Start offset in seconds, if the link had one. */
  startSeconds?: number;
  /** Best guess before the player loads; the adapter reports the truth. */
  maybeLive: boolean;
}

/** A link we recognized but can't play (e.g. a @handle live URL without a video id). */
export interface ParseProblem {
  providerId: string;
  message: string;
}

export interface ProviderCapabilities {
  /** Whether the provider's terms let us draw captions on top of its embedded player. */
  allowsCaptionOverlay: boolean;
  /** Smallest player viewport the provider allows, in CSS px. */
  minPlayerSize: { width: number; height: number };
}

export type PlayerState = "unstarted" | "playing" | "paused" | "buffering" | "ended";

export interface PlayerError {
  code: string;
  message: string;
  /** Embedding refused by the uploader: offer to open the video on the provider's site. */
  embeddingBlocked: boolean;
}

export interface PlayerEvents {
  onReady?: () => void;
  onStateChange?: (state: PlayerState) => void;
  onError?: (error: PlayerError) => void;
}

/** What the watch page needs from a player, whatever the provider. */
export interface PlayerAdapter {
  getCurrentTime(): number;
  seekTo(seconds: number): void;
  play(): void;
  getState(): PlayerState;
  isLive(): boolean;
  getTitle(): string | null;
  getPlaybackRate(): number;
  destroy(): void;
}

export interface VideoProvider {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  capabilities: ProviderCapabilities;
  /** Returns the parsed video, a problem explaining why it can't be played, or null if not ours. */
  parse(url: URL): ParsedVideo | ParseProblem | null;
  /** Mount a player inside `host`. The player lives in its own child element, removed on destroy. */
  mount(host: HTMLElement, video: ParsedVideo, events: PlayerEvents): Promise<PlayerAdapter>;
}

export function isParseProblem(v: ParsedVideo | ParseProblem): v is ParseProblem {
  return "message" in v;
}

I ran one search. It covers the `parent` parameter well, but it doesn't confirm `getCurrentTime` on Twitch's player, and it has nothing on a developer agreement overlay.

**The `parent` parameter:** Twitch's 2020 developer update says sites embedding Twitch need to list their domains in `parent`, which helps avoid Twitch content on your site being blocked by modern browsers. For JavaScript embeds, the parent key goes in the options object used to configure the embed, and its value is a JavaScript array of the domains that embed your content. The docs give the same pattern for `Twitch.Embed`, using parent: ["embed.example.com", "othersite.example.com"]. A forum user also reports that the NoParent error appears when trying to embed an Interactive Frame without a parent.

**Playback control and `getCurrentTime`:** Twitch's video-and-clips docs list a volume API and a status API (such as `getPlaybackStats()`), but the excerpt doesn't show a `getCurrentTime` call. Forum threads from earlier years ask for a way to read the current time from the embedded player, and one developer says there isn't one currently, as far as they believe, though Twitch has been working on a better JavaScript interface. Treat `getCurrentTime` on Twitch as unconfirmed by these results. The docs also show that you can reach the player through getPlayer(), which retrieves the current video player instance from the embed.

**Developer agreement overlay:** None of the results mention an overlay or a developer agreement. If that part matters, it needs a separate search against Twitch's developer terms.

content.text:
The answer depends on which part of Heard you mean.

## Chrome extension: probably already works on all five
The extension doesn't know which site it's on. It captures the tab's audio with `tabCapture`, and the caption box attaches to the largest `<video>` on the page ([Overlay.tsx:77](apps/extension/entrypoints/overlay.content/Overlay.tsx:77)). All five platforms play live streams in a desktop browser using a normal `<video>`, so this should be mostly testing, not new code. I haven't tried any of them. Things to check:
- **TikTok Live and IG Live are vertical video.** The caption box is 82% of the video's width with a minimum size, so it may spill past a narrow 9:16 frame.
- **Fullscreen:** each site uses its own fullscreen setup, and the overlay needs to move into whichever element is fullscreen.
- **Muted autoplay** (X, LinkedIn, IG): if the player is muted, Heard hears silence.
- **Store listing / i18n text** says "YouTube" in places, so the copy would need widening.

## Web app (paste a link, watch with captions)
This needs an embeddable player for each platform:

| Platform | Official live embed? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Twitch** | Yes. The `Twitch.Player` JS API covers live channels and past broadcasts (VODs), with play/pause/seek and ONLINE/OFFLINE/ENDED events | **Doable**, as a new `VideoProvider` |
| LinkedIn Live | No. Only third-party widgets | Extension only |
| X Live | No. Posts can be embedded, live broadcasts can't | Extension only |
| TikTok Live | No. The oEmbed endpoint covers regular videos and profiles, not LIVE | Extension only |
| IG Live | No public live embed found | Extension only |

The web app only gets one platform out of the five; the extension covers all of them.

**Twitch caveats** (these would go in [docs/provider-policies.md](docs/provider-policies.md)):
- **No captions over the player.** Twitch's rule 1.3 says embeds "should not be obscured in any way", so `allowsCaptionOverlay: false`, the same caption bar below the player that YouTube uses.
- **Minimum player size** is 400×300 (YouTube's is 200×200).
- **`parent` domain and HTTPS:** each embed must name the site's domain in `parent`, and the site must use HTTPS. Local dev on `127.0.0.1` needs checking.
- **No playback time on live streams.** `getCurrentTime` and `seek` only work on past broadcasts. On a live stream, transcript timestamps would need to come from the clock instead. Clips have no JS API at all.
- Twitch's Developer Services Agreement may add more rules; I didn't read it.

Sources: [Twitch: Embedding Video and Clips](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/video-and-clips/), [Twitch: Embed overview](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/), [TikTok embed docs](https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/embed-videos), [X embedded posts](https://docs.x.com/x-for-websites/embedded-posts/overview), [LinkedIn Live help](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/100224)

input.content:
# Plan: supporting more streaming platforms

Status: draft, 2026-11-28. Covers Twitch, LinkedIn Live, X (Twitter) Live, TikTok Live and
Instagram Live.

Heard runs in two places, and each needs different work:

| Surface | How it captures | What a new platform needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Chrome extension** (`apps/extension`) | `tabCapture` on whatever tab you're on. The caption box attaches to the page's largest `<video>`. | Usually nothing in capture or transcription. Test the overlay on each site and fix what breaks. |
| **Web app** (`apps/web`) | Embeds the provider's player and captures the tab with `getDisplayMedia`. | An official, embeddable player and a `VideoProvider` in `apps/web/src/lib/providers/`. |

## Summary

| Platform | Extension | Web app | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Twitch | Test and polish | **Add a provider** | Official `Twitch.Player` JS API for live channels and VODs |
| LinkedIn Live | Test and polish | Not supported. Point to the extension | No official live embed |
| X Live | Test and polish | Not supported. Point to the extension | X embeds posts, not broadcasts |
| TikTok Live | Test and polish (vertical video) | Not supported. Point to the extension | oEmbed covers videos and profiles, not LIVE |
| Instagram Live | Test and polish (vertical video) | Not supported. Point to the extension | No public live embed |

So the work has three tracks. Each one can ship by itself:

1. **Extension: verify and harden on all five sites** (biggest reach, least code).
2. **Web app: Twitch provider** (the only new embed).
3. **Web app: recognize the other four links** and send people to the extension instead of
   "Heard doesn't recognize that link".

---

## Track 1: Extension on all five platforms

No permission changes. The extension keeps its minimal permission set (`tabCapture`,
`offscreen`, `sidePanel`, `storage`, `activeTab`, `scripting`, no host permissions), which
`verify-store-package.mjs` enforces. Don't add per-site host permissions or always-on content
scripts for this work.

### 1.1 Manual test pass

Add one section per platform to the manual checklist in `apps/extension/README.md`, matching
the existing "YouTube livestream" section:

| Platform | Test URL shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Twitch | `twitch.tv/<channel>` (live), `twitch.tv/videos/<id>` (VOD) | Theater mode, fullscreen, ads at the start (separate `<video>`?), channel raids that navigate in-page |
| LinkedIn Live | `linkedin.com/events/...`, `linkedin.com/video/live/urn:li:ugcPost:...`, live post in the feed | The feed has many `<video>`s; check the box picks the live one. Autoplay starts muted. |
| X Live | `x.com/i/broadcasts/<id>`, live post in the timeline | Starts muted; the broadcast page has chat beside the video |
| TikTok Live | `tiktok.com/@<user>/live` | 9:16 video, comments and gifts drawn over the video |
| Instagram Live | `instagram.com/<user>/live` (desktop web, signed in) | 9:16 video, comments drawn over the video |

For each one, check:

- [ ] Captions start after clicking the toolbar icon; `LIVE` badge shows.
- [ ] Caption box sits on the right video and follows it when scrolling or changing layout.
- [ ] Fullscreen (the site's own button): the box stays visible.
- [ ] Clicks on the player and page outside the box still work.
- [ ] Muted player: we show a clear hint instead of silently producing nothing (see 1.3).
- [ ] In-page navigation to another stream: captions keep flowing or stop cleanly.
- [ ] Stop: badge clears, no leftover overlay.

### 1.2 Vertical video (TikTok, Instagram)

`onVideo()` in `apps/extension/entrypoints/overlay.content/Overlay.tsx` sizes the box at 82% of
the video's width, with a `MIN_WIDTH` floor, and scales the font by video height. On a narrow
9:16 player this can overflow the frame or produce very large text.

- Detect portrait video (`height > width`).
- Base font scale on width for portrait video, and allow the box to be wider than the video
  when needed, centered on it.
- Consider placing the box above the bottom ~25% of the frame, where TikTok and Instagram draw
  comments and the input bar.

### 1.3 Muted playback hint

X, LinkedIn and Instagram autoplay muted. Tab capture then records silence and the user sees
no captions. Ideas, cheapest first:

- If Deepgram returns nothing for N seconds and the main `<video>` has `muted` or
  `volume === 0`, show "Unmute the video to get captions" in the caption box.
- This only reads the `<video>` element the overlay already tracks; no new permissions.

### 1.4 Main-video detection

`findMainVideo` picks the largest visible `<video>`, playing ones first. Feeds (LinkedIn, X)
can contain several playing previews. If testing shows wrong picks, prefer the video that has
audio (not muted) and is closest to the viewport center. Keep it generic; avoid per-site
selectors unless a site truly needs one.

### 1.5 Copy and store listing

- Extension README intro already says it isn't site-specific; add the five platforms as
  examples.
- Review `docs/chrome-web-store-listing.md` and `public/_locales/*/messages.json` for
  YouTube-only wording. Store copy must not claim affiliation with any platform; naming them
  as examples ("works on Twitch, LinkedIn Live, …") is fine but check each brand's naming
  rules before it goes into the listing.

### 1.6 Policies

Add a short section per platform to `docs/provider-policies.md` covering the extension
use-case (user's own browser, user-initiated tab capture, nothing stored or redistributed),
the same way the YouTube section covers it. Note any terms that mention automated access or
recording, so the owner can decide before a store release.

---

## Track 2: Twitch provider for the web app

Source: [Twitch: Embedding Video and Clips](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/video-and-clips/),
[Twitch: Embed overview](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/).

### 2.1 What Twitch offers

- `Twitch.Player` JS API (`https://player.twitch.tv/js/embed/v1.js`) for **live channels**
  (`channel`) and **VODs** (`video`, `v`-prefixed id).
- Methods: `play()`, `pause()`, `seek()`, `getCurrentTime()`, `getEnded()`, `getChannel()`,
  `getVideo()`.
- Events: `READY`, `PLAY`, `PLAYING`, `PAUSE`, `ENDED`, `ONLINE`, `OFFLINE`,
  `PLAYBACK_BLOCKED`, `SEEK`.
- `getCurrentTime()` and `seek()` **work only for VODs**, not live streams.
- **Clips** (`clips.twitch.tv/...`, `twitch.tv/<ch>/clip/...`) only have a plain iframe with no
  JS API.

### 2.2 Rules that shape the design

| Rule | Effect on Heard |
|---|---|
| Embeds "should not be obscured in any way" (rule 1.3) | `allowsCaptionOverlay: false`. Captions go in the bar below the player, as for YouTube. |
| "Must utilize only Twitch-approved player elements" | Don't hide or restyle Twitch's controls. Heard's fullscreen wraps player + caption bar, like YouTube. |
| Minimum 400×300 | `minPlayerSize: { width: 400, height: 300 }`. Check the mobile/narrow layout honors it. |
| `parent` must list the embedding domain | Pass `window.location.hostname`. Verify `127.0.0.1` works for local dev. |
| HTTPS required | Fine for deployments; check local dev over HTTP on loopback. If Twitch refuses it, document the workaround. |

Read the Twitch Developer Services Agreement before shipping and record the findings in
`docs/provider-policies.md` under a new "Twitch" section.

### 2.3 Implementation

New files, following `providers/youtube/`:

```
apps/web/src/lib/providers/twitch/
  embed-api.ts   # load player.twitch.tv/js/embed/v1.js once, typed Twitch.Player
  parse.ts       # URL → ParsedVideo | ParseProblem
  index.ts       # twitchProvider: capabilities, parse, mount → PlayerAdapter
```

Register it in `PROVIDERS` in `apps/web/src/lib/providers/index.ts` and update the
"doesn't recognize that link" message and the `UrlForm` placeholder / i18n strings.

**Parsing**

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `twitch.tv/<channel>` | live channel, `maybeLive: true` |
| `twitch.tv/videos/<id>` (`?t=1h2m3s`) | VOD, `startSeconds` from `t` |
| `m.twitch.tv/...`, `www.twitch.tv/...` | same as above |
| `twitch.tv/<channel>/clip/<slug>`, `clips.twitch.tv/<slug>` | `ParseProblem`: clips aren't supported yet (no JS API); suggest the extension |
| `twitch.tv/directory/...`, `/settings`, other reserved paths | `null` or `ParseProblem` |

**Adapter**

- `getCurrentTime()`: for VODs, the player's time. For live, return a value the watch page
  treats as "no media time" so transcript lines aren't seekable. `StreamTimeMap` and
  `getMediaTime` already accept `null`; check `WatchExperience.tsx` handles a provider that
  never reports live time (the YouTube live path reports a DVR time instead).
- `seekTo()`: VOD only; no-op for live.
- `isLive()`: true when `channel` was used and the stream is `ONLINE`.
- `getState()`: map `PLAY`/`PLAYING` → playing, `PAUSE` → paused, `ENDED`/`OFFLINE` → ended.
- `getTitle()`: channel name or VOD id (the embed API doesn't expose titles; don't add the
  Helix API, which needs a client id).
- Errors: `OFFLINE` at start → friendly "This channel isn't live right now" with
  "Open on Twitch"; `PLAYBACK_BLOCKED` → prompt to press play.

**Content Security Policy:** if `apps/web/src/proxy.ts` or `next.config.ts` sets a CSP, allow
`player.twitch.tv` (script + frame) and `embed.twitch.tv`.

### 2.4 Tests

- Unit tests for `parse.ts` (all URL shapes above, `t=` parsing, clips, reserved paths).
- Extend `apps/web/scripts/e2e.mjs` with an optional Twitch VOD run (live channels are
  unpredictable in CI).
- Manual: one live channel, one VOD with `?t=`, one offline channel, one clip link.

---

## Track 3: Recognize the other links in the web app

LinkedIn Live, X Live, TikTok Live and Instagram Live have no official embed, so the web app
can't play them. Today a pasted link gets the generic "doesn't recognize that link" message.

Add parse-only providers (or one `externalOnly` list) that match these hosts and return a
`ParseProblem` with a clear message, for example:

> "LinkedIn Live can't be embedded here. Open it on LinkedIn and use the Heard Chrome
> extension to caption it."

with an "Open on LinkedIn" link and the extension install link. Hosts to match:
`linkedin.com`, `x.com` / `twitter.com`, `tiktok.com`, `instagram.com`.

Don't scrape, proxy or re-host any of these streams to get around the missing embed.

---

## Order of work

1. **Track 1.1** test pass on all five sites. Record what breaks.
2. **Track 3**: small, and immediately improves the web app's message.
3. **Track 1.2–1.4** fixes for whatever 1.1 found (vertical video likely).
4. **Track 2** Twitch provider, after reading the Twitch Developer Services Agreement.
5. **Track 1.5–1.6** copy, store listing and policy doc updates, before the next store
   release.

## Out of scope for now

- Twitch clips on the web app (no JS API).
- Mobile apps for any platform (no tab capture on mobile browsers).
- Using platform APIs that need sign-in or a client id (Twitch Helix, X API, Meta Graph).
- Changing who pays for Deepgram usage: the `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` rules in `AGENTS.md` apply
  unchanged to every platform.

## Open questions

- Does Twitch's `parent` check accept `127.0.0.1` over HTTP for local dev?
- Do any of the five platforms' terms restrict capturing or transcribing a stream's audio in
  the viewer's own browser? (Same open question as YouTube Developer Policy III.I.7.)
- Is it worth a per-site tweak for TikTok and Instagram so the caption box avoids their
  comment overlay, or is the generic portrait-video rule enough?

The work is in three tracks, and each can ship on its own:

1. **Extension on all five sites.** Capture already works on any site, so this is mostly testing. The plan adds a checklist for each platform to the extension README and lists the fixes I expect to need:
   - **Vertical video:** the caption box sizing doesn't fit TikTok or Instagram's 9:16 player.

124:See [docs/provider-policies.md](docs/provider-policies.md). YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality forbids overlays in front of an embedded player. 126:## Known limitations
127:
128:- **Browsers:** desktop Chrome/Edge only. Firefox and Safari don't support tab-audio capture through `getDisplayMedia`, and mobile browsers have no tab capture.
129:- **Caption delay:** captions lag speech by roughly 0.3–1 s (network plus recognition). The video isn't delayed to compensate.
130:- **Embedding:** videos whose owners disable embedding (YouTube errors 101/150) can't play on the web platform; use the extension on youtube.com instead. `youtube.com/@handle/live` links can't be resolved without the YouTube Data API, so paste the video link.

## Twitch

Checked 2026-11-28 against:

- Embedding Twitch — https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/
- Embedding Video and Clips — https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/embed/video-and-clips/

Not yet read: the Twitch Developer Services Agreement, which the embed docs point to. Read it
before a public deployment.

### Captions over the player: not allowed

Embed rule 1.3 says embeds "should not be obscured in any way by other page elements" and
must use only Twitch-approved player elements. So
`twitchProvider.capabilities.allowsCaptionOverlay = false`, and Twitch gets the same
treatment as YouTube: caption bar below the player, no "Over video" option, Heard's own
fullscreen wraps the untouched player plus the caption bar.

### Player size

Embedded players "must be at least 400x300 pixels"; `minPlayerSize` is 400×300 and the watch
page applies it as `min-width`/`min-height`. On screens narrower than 400px the page scrolls
sideways rather than shrinking the player below the minimum.

### `parent` and HTTPS

The player only plays on domains listed in `parent`; Heard passes `window.location.hostname`.
Twitch says embedding domains must use SSL. Tested 2026-11-28: the local dev server on
`http://127.0.0.1:3100` loads and plays a live channel, so local development needs no
certificate. Public deployments are HTTPS anyway.

### What the API supports

- Live channels (`channel`) and past broadcasts (`video`) through `Twitch.Player`.
- `getCurrentTime()` and `seek()` work only for past broadcasts. For live channels the adapter
  reports `hasTimeline() === false`, so transcript lines use capture time and aren't
  clickable.
- Clips only have a plain iframe with no JS API, so the web app turns clip links away and
  points to the extension.

### Open question: audio capture

Same as YouTube: Heard transcribes the tab's audio in the viewer's own browser, after Chrome's
tab-sharing prompt, and doesn't store or redistribute it. Whether Twitch's terms address this
hasn't been checked.

## LinkedIn Live, X Live, TikTok Live, Instagram Live

Checked 2026-11-28: none of these offers an official embed for live streams (LinkedIn and X
embed posts; TikTok's oEmbed covers videos and profiles, not LIVE; Instagram has no live
embed). The web app therefore doesn't play them. Pasted links get a message that links to the
stream on the platform's own site and to the extension
(`apps/web/src/lib/providers/extension-only.ts`). Never scrape, proxy or re-host these streams
to get around the missing embed.

The Chrome extension captions them on the platforms' own sites, the same way it does on
youtube.com: the viewer starts capture on their own tab, audio goes only to Deepgram, nothing
is stored or redistributed, and the caption box is drawn by the extension in the viewer's
browser (no embedded-player rules apply).

Open question: none of these platforms' terms have been reviewed for automated access or
transcription of stream audio. Review them, as for YouTube III.I.7, before naming the
platforms in the Chrome Web Store listing or a public announcement.

Twitch's rules don't allow anything on top of its player, so captions show in the bar below it and the player is never smaller than 400×300.
- I tested a live Twitch channel in the browser on your local dev server, and it plays.
- **Live Twitch transcripts use capture time:** Twitch only reports the playback position for past broadcasts, so you can't click a live line to jump in the video.
- **Clip links** are turned away with an explanation, because Twitch's clip player can't be controlled from another site.
- **LinkedIn, X, TikTok and Instagram links** now say the platform doesn't allow embedding. They link to the stream and to the extension instead of "doesn't recognize that link" ([extension-only.ts](apps/web/src/lib/providers/extension-only.ts)). I checked this in English and Spanish.

**Extension**
- **Vertical video (TikTok, Instagram):** the caption box is centered on the video and sits higher, clear of the comments area. Text no longer grows too big in a tall, narrow player.
- **Muted video:** when the video is playing with the sound off, the box says "Unmute the video to get captions."
- **Feeds with several videos (LinkedIn, X):** the box goes on the video that's playing with sound and near the middle of the screen, not just the biggest one.
- This logic is in [video-geometry.ts](apps/extension/utils/video-geometry.ts) and works the same on every site. The extension still asks for no extra permissions.

**Your open questions**
- **Local Twitch playback:** answered. The player works on `127.0.0.1` over plain HTTP, so you don't need a certificate for local development.
- **Platform terms:** still open. I noted in [provider-policies.md](docs/provider-policies.md) that the terms should be read before you name these platforms in the Chrome Web Store listing or announce support.
- **TikTok and Instagram comments:** whether the raised caption position is enough will show up during the manual test.
